notes: §1985:VI.6.24.4 GR4: "If STOP literal-1 is specified, the execution of the run unit is suspended and literal-1 is communicated to the operator. Continuation of the execution of the run unit begins with the next executable statement when the implementor-defined procedure governing run unit reinitiation is instituted." VisitStopStatement is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85, COBOL0902 from 2002); BindStop binds the statement to BoundStopLiteral, and StatementEmitter's Visit overload for that node writes the text to the standard error stream and falls through to the next statement. Conforming, read and probed at 85: a nonnumeric and a numeric literal reach the operator channel, and execution continues with the next statement in a sentence, inside an IF and in a performed paragraph. Diverging: BindStop decodes the SOURCE TEXT of literal-1, so a figurative constant is communicated as its word (STOP ZERO writes ZERO, STOP SPACE writes SPACE, STOP QUOTE writes QUOTE) where the rule communicates literal-1, the constant's one-character value (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3); kb/Work PB5074 holds this. A second point is a reading, not counted in the verdict: the run unit is never suspended. The statement returns at once, which docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3 (D-SEQ) and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.11 state as the implementor-defined reinitiation procedure (§1985:C.2 item 41), and which no kb/Work note questions; GnuCOBOL 3.2 at -std=cobol85 displays the literal and then waits for operator input (measured: cob_display followed by cob_accept). The witness displays a line before and after STOP "PAUSE" and reads standard output only.

next.reason: 1985: "If STOP literal-1 is specified, the execution of the run unit is suspended and literal-1 is communicated to the operator."; 2023: "Format is only STOP RUN [WITH ERROR/NORMAL STATUS literal-1]; "Execution of the run unit terminates"". The 2023 STOP format offers only STOP RUN. The suspend-and-resume STOP literal-1 is gone. A literal in WITH STATUS is passed to the OS at termination, not shown to an operator awaiting resumption.
